google_calendar.title: Set up Google for this server
steps: Open the Google Cloud console, choose your project and enable the Google Calendar API (APIs & Services → Library).
On the OAuth consent screen add the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly. While the app is in testing mode, add your team as test users.
On your OAuth client (the one used for Google sign-in) add this authorised redirect URI:
Put the client ID and secret into the server settings: LK_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and LK_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, set LK_PUBLIC_URL to this site's address, and restart the server.
Come back to this page and press Connect.

github.name: GitHub
github.tagline: Link projects to repositories: pull requests and issues show up on tasks, merges move them, and both sides follow each other.
github.adminOnly: Only owners and administrators can connect or change GitHub.
steps: On GitHub open Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens and create a token.

Give it the scopes repo and admin:repo_hook (a fine-grained token also works: read & write for Issues, Pull requests and Webhooks, plus read for Contents and Metadata, on the repositories you will link).
Paste the token below and press Connect. It is checked, then stored encrypted.
Link each project to its repository. The webhook is created for you; it must reach this server, so LK_PUBLIC_URL has to be the public address.
Mention a task key such as PLT-12 in a pull request title, branch name or description to link it to the task.
github.tokenHint: Needs the repo and admin:repo_hook scopes. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.

rules.prOpenedToReviewHint: A pull request that mentions a task moves it to In review (never backwards from Done).
rules.prMergedToDoneHint: Merging finishes the tasks it mentions.
rules.syncIssuesHint: A new issue becomes a task; closing it finishes the task; moving a task to Done closes its issue, and back out of Done reopens it.
rules.commentOnPrHint: Moving a task adds a comment with a link on its open pull requests.

github.webhookHint: Created on each linked repository automatically. It must be reachable from the internet.
github.howItWorks: Changes made by these rules appear as made by the person who connected GitHub. Task keys are matched in pull request titles, branch names and descriptions.
github.disconnectBody: The webhooks are removed, and the token, linked repositories and task links are deleted. Nothing changes on GitHub.
